```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

**BlockR** is a drag-and-drop canvas on top of
[teal](https://insightsengineering.github.io/teal/): it lets people who do
not write R build clinical tables, listings and graphs from blocks, starting
from any output of the
[TLG Catalog](https://insightsengineering.github.io/tlg-catalog/stable/tlg-index.html).

## Run the app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(BlockR)
run_app()
```

From the project folder you can also open `app.R` in RStudio and press
**Run App** (it loads the package with `pkgload` and calls `run_app()`).

The first launch builds the data (a few seconds); later launches in the same
R session are served from memory, and new sessions from the disk cache.

## A tour of the app

| Tab | What it shows | Starting population |
|---|---|---|
| Canvas | The home page: build outputs from blocks; its **Tutorial** button opens eight lessons on a canvas of their own | All subjects (each template filters its own population, with a block) |
| TLG Catalog | Every table, listing and graph of the TLG Catalog, on one page | As in the catalog (per output) |
| Data Table, Variable Browser | All datasets | All subjects |
| Exploratory Analysis | Distributions, outliers, associations, regression, PCA, ... | All subjects |
| Safety Analysis | Demographics, adverse events, labs, exposure, vitals, ECG, concomitant medication | Safety population (`SAFFL == "Y"`) |

* **Filters.** Sex and age filters apply everywhere; each safety module also
  starts on the safety population, as in its source template. On the canvas
  the filter panel is folded at first (open it with `\`).
* **Show R code** on any page gives runnable code (on the canvas, the
  canvas's own *Show R code* button): it starts with
  `BlockR::load_blockr_data()` with the data-source settings written out, so it
  reproduces the same data in a fresh R session.
* **Dark mode**: the sun/moon button in the header switches the whole app
  between light and dark colours; the browser remembers your choice.

## The canvas

New to it? Press the bright **Tutorial** button at the top right of the
canvas: eight short lessons, on a canvas of their own, from the first click
(Beginner) to wiring a table by hand and writing a little R (Advanced). Each
step is ticked as soon as you have done it; *Show me* points at what to use.
*Back to my canvas* returns to yours, as you left it. And every part of the page and every block has a
small **?**: click it to know what it is, or what the block does here.

### Start

On an empty canvas, pick one of the featured templates, *Browse all
templates* (the *Templates* tab of the palette, searchable by ID or title),
or *Start from a dataset*. On the TLG Catalog page, **Open in Canvas** does
the same for the output you are looking at.

### Read it

* A **stack** of blocks is a pipeline, read from top to bottom: *ADAE*, then
  *Filter rows* (SAFFL is Y and ANL01FL is Y), then *Show missing values*.
  Each block works on the result of the block above it.
* The footer of each block says what it produces: `1,586 rows · 98 cols`
  (and `-348` when it removed rows), `table · 24 rows × 4 cols`, `plot`...
* **Wires** bring the result of a stack to a block that uses it, for
  example the rows, the layout and the column counts of *Build table*. The
  number on a wire is the number of rows travelling on it.
* The ★ **Result** block is the one shown in the *Result* panel: by default
  the template's result (or the last table, listing or plot).
* A block that has a problem turns red and says why; the blocks after it
  wait, and everything else keeps working.

### Change it

* **Settings**: click a block. Its settings open in the *Block* panel, with
  what the block produces below them. Conditions are rows of
  *column · is · value* (the values of the column to choose from); columns
  are tags; labels are pairs; anything else is R code.
* **Add**: drag a block from the palette onto the canvas, between or below
  blocks of a stack; or click it to add it below the selected block.
* **+**: the button under a stack suggests what to do next with its result.
  For rows: filter, derive, order, count, or a ready-made *Summary table by
  arm*, *Patients per value by arm*, *Listing* or *Plot*, with all their
  blocks added and wired; for a table layout: its columns, rows and
  statistics, or *Build the table*; for a plot: layers.
* **Move**: drag a block (the gap closes); shift-drag to take the blocks
  below it too; drag the first block of a stack to move the whole stack.
* **Connect**: drag from the round port under a stack to a socket (or click
  a socket and choose).
* **Bypass** (right-click, or the *Bypass* button): skip a block without
  deleting it, for example to see the table without a filter.
* **Undo** everything with `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on a Mac).

### Make room

The canvas fills the window below the header. Fold the palette (first
toolbar button) or the right panel (next to last), drag the panel's left
edge to resize it, or show the canvas **full screen** (last button; Esc
leaves). The **?** buttons can be hidden: *Appearance* (the sliders in the
header) → *"What is this?" tips* → Hide, or the `···` menu of the canvas.

### Keep it

The canvas is saved in your browser. Click its title to rename it; the `···`
menu exports it as a file (to share it, or open it later with *Import*) and
copies or downloads its R code. The *Code* panel shows the code of the canvas
as you build it, and **Show R code** gives the complete script, including the
loading of the data and the app's filters.

### R and SAS code, both ways

* The *Code* panel's **R / SAS** switch shows the canvas as SAS code: DATA
  steps, PROC SQL, MEANS, REPORT, SGPLOT, LIFETEST. It is a translation for
  SAS users: what has no SAS equivalent is marked `TODO` with its R code, and
  the results should be checked against the R output. Copy and Download
  follow the switch (`.sas`).
* **Edit** (in the Code panel) turns the R code into a text box: change it
  and press *Draw the blocks* (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter): the canvas is redrawn from
  your code.
* **Paste R code** (the `···` menu, the empty canvas, or simply Ctrl/Cmd+V on
  the canvas): your own R code becomes blocks, replacing the canvas or added
  to it. For example

  ```r
  adae <- ADAE %>% filter(AESER == "Y")
  result <- adae %>% count(AEBODSYS, sort = TRUE)
  ```

  gives an *ADAE* block, a *Filter rows* block and a *Count rows* block.
  If the code cannot be read, the line with the problem is shown.

## The TLG Catalog

The **TLG Catalog** page reproduces the outputs of the
[TLG Catalog](https://insightsengineering.github.io/tlg-catalog/stable/tlg-index.html)
on the app's data, grouped by topic (Adverse Events, Concomitant Medications,
Lab Results, Efficacy, Pharmacokinetics, ...) in one searchable list. Select
an output (click, or use the arrow keys) to compute it on the filtered data.

* **Open in Canvas** turns the output into blocks.
* **Show R code** gives the complete code: the data loading, the filters and
  the output's code, written in the catalog's style (tern, rtables, rlistings).
* **Catalog** opens the output's page in the TLG Catalog.
* A few outputs need datasets the app does not load (ADPC, ADPP, ADAB, ADMH,
  ADHY); they use the *random.cdisc.data* examples for the same patients, as
  noted on their page.

## The data in the console

`run_app()` copies every analysis dataset into the Global Environment, so after
closing the app you can explore them directly:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
head(ADSL)
table(ADAE$AEDECOD)
```

Without the app:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bk <- load_blockr_data(cache_global = TRUE)
names(bk$datasets)
```

Turn the copy off with `options(blockr.cache_global = FALSE)` or
`run_app(cache_global = FALSE)`.

## Settings

Everything is configured with R options (see `?blockr_options`) or the
equivalent arguments of `run_app()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# freshly generated synthetic data: 200 subjects, seed 7
run_app(source = "synthetic", synthetic = list(N = 200, seed = 7))

# your own ADaM data as parquet files
run_app(source = "parquet", parquet_dir = "path/to/adam")

# force a rebuild of the cached data
options(blockr.refresh_cache = TRUE)
```

See `vignette("data-sources", package = "BlockR")` for the data sources, the
data contract and the cache.

## Look and feel

The app keeps teal's structure and its standard Bootstrap 5 theme. A
stylesheet and one script on top of it add:

* **A home page**: the canvas; click the logo (or press `H`) to come back
  to it.
* **A command bar**: press `Ctrl+K` (`Cmd+K` on a Mac), `/`, or click the
  search field in the header. Before you type, *Where to?* shows every
  module in its category, nested as in the menus. Type a few letters of a module
  (`km`, `ae grade`), a TLG output ID (`aet02`) or an action (`>dark`).
  `Enter` opens it; `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` opens it in a new browser tab.
* **Where am I**: the header shows the path of the current module (for
  example *Safety Analysis / Adverse Events / AE Summary*); click a part of it
  to see the other modules of that group.
* **Links to every view**: the address bar follows the app
  (`.../#/safety-analysis/adverse-events/ae-summary`), so views can be bookmarked
  and shared, and the browser's back button goes to the previous view.
* **Output tools**: hover a plot to expand it (zoom with the wheel, drag to
  pan), pin it, compare it, copy it or download it; hover a table to copy it
  for Excel or download it as CSV.
* **Comparison**: pin a plot, change a filter, then choose *Compare*: swipe
  a divider between the two versions, put them side by side, or show their
  difference (what changed keeps its colour, the rest turns white). Pins stay
  in a tray (`P`) for the session.
* **Keyboard shortcuts** for everything; press `?` to see them.
* **A calm, precise look** ("Instrument"): ruled white panels on a dot-grid
  canvas, one teal accent, the system font (Inter elsewhere) for text and
  JetBrains Mono for dataset names, IDs and numbers; a quiet tint per
  category (blue for Exploratory, terracotta for Safety, violet for the TLG
  Catalog); a dark mode that works.
* **Appearance** (the sliders button, or `A`): text size, spacing, accent,
  corners, contrast, canvas and motion, remembered by the browser.
* **Plots**: an editorial look for every ggplot2 module (large titles, facet
  labels as headings, a graded ink scale, no tick marks) and
  `theme_minimal()` as the default theme of the exploratory plots. Both are
  applied through teal's own settings, so "Show R code" reproduces the plots
  exactly. In dark mode, plots stay white paper.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(blockr.color_mode = "dark")  # default mode for first-time visitors ("light")
options(blockr.motion = FALSE)       # no animations
options(blockr.ggtheme = "bw")       # another default plot theme (NULL: module defaults)
options(blockr.style = FALSE)        # the plain teal look of the source templates
```

To change the plot typography, set teal's own option, which BlockR then
leaves alone:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
options(teal.ggplot2_args = teal.widgets::ggplot2_args(
  labs = list(caption = "MY STUDY"),
  theme = blockr_plot_theme_args()
))
```
